fatal_errors: The cited evidence concerns a spray-coated steel-on-steel contact tested in ambient conditions and does not support operation on CoCrFeNi up to 800 °C.

The hypothesis assumes that a sulfide nanoflake coating and its tribocatalytic film remain lubricious throughout oxidative high-temperature sliding without addressing oxidation, depletion, or coating-substrate reactions.
The proposed intervention and bare-alloy baseline do not reconstruct the target Mo-varied CoCrFeNiMox-Ni/MoS2-Ag-Cr2O3 composite system.
The claim of coefficient of friction below 0.1 across the entire temperature and load range is unsupported by the cited room-temperature evidence.
explanation: The response identifies one clear intervention and directly addresses friction and wear over room temperature to 800 °C, so it is aligned with the general engineering problem and is reasonably novel. It is not a reconstruction of the target study, which varied Mo content in a multiphase SPS composite and relied on solid-solution/σ-phase strengthening plus temperature-dependent MoS2, Ag, oxide, and silver-molybdate films. The cited study supports low friction for the proposed coating on steel at one high load in ambient conditions, but it provides no evidence for CoCrFeNi compatibility or survival at 200–800 °C. Conditions and boundaries are also too vague: counterface, speed, distance, discrete loads, humidity, coating thickness, and thermal exposure are unspecified. The coated-versus-uncoated experiment is directionally discriminating and includes tribofilm characterization, but it needs fixed test parameters, replication, and temperature-specific pass/fail criteria. Its falsification rule also mixes an absolute COF threshold, relative improvement, wear, and film observation in an ambiguous way.
